testId: testim-migrated/tests/webstore/login/verify-validation-on-login-page.spec.ts > Webstore - Login > verify validation on login page

scenario.summary: Guest opens the sign-in panel and checks its validations: empty submit (required username and password messages), focusing the empty username, a registered username with a wrong password, and a non-existent username with a password.
steps: Open '/' as a guest (storageState empty); header Sign In
Click Sign In with both fields empty; check the required-username and required-password messages
Click the empty username field; check the sign-in error text
Fill the account's username and a wrong password (invalidPassword); Sign In; check the sign-in error
Fill a non-existent username (invalidUserName) and the password; Sign In; check 'The entered Username or Password does not exist.' (SignInValidationMessage)
stateChanges: One failed sign-in attempt (wrong password) against the declared account per run: it may count toward a failed-attempt lockout (not checked; usually reset by the next successful sign-in, which other specs of the shared account do); repeated runs without a successful sign-in could lock the shared account (REVIEW)
The non-existent-username attempt touches no account
assertions: signInError has text emptyUsernameBoxErrorMessage (empty username focused)
signInError has text wrongUsernameErrorMessage (registered username + wrong password)
evidence: Title 'verify validation on login page' and the step labels match the flow

DECLARED ACCOUNT: source 4 (keyPath username, masked by key name) is typed into the sign-in username field in the step 'Valid username + wrong password' (usedBy step 8), so it is a registered account's username: role credential, alias user, preferred.required true. Source 8 (keyPath password, masked by key name) is typed with the non-existent username in the step 'Non-existent username + valid password' (usedBy step 13): by its name and the step label it is the account's real password -> credential, alias user (kept in the spec's JSON; the check would pass with any password, the migrated spec may keep reading it). user -> USER_WEBSTORE_REGISTERED {store}; the migrated test declares it with await testData.useExisting('user', data.username) before its first sign-in attempt

Invalid values the test types (config, never a real account): source 5 (keyPath invalidPassword, masked by key name) is the wrong password typed with the registered username; source 7 (keyPath invalidUserName, masked by key name) is the non-existent username. Both are fixed recorded literals; the migrated spec should generate the non-existent username per run (e.g. a unique run-tagged name that is never registered) and may generate the wrong password; no key is needed

Masked validation messages, not credentials (masked only because the key contains 'password'/'username'): source 1 wrongPasswordErrorMessage, source 2 emptyPasswordBoxErrorMessage, source 3 emptyUsernameBoxErrorMessage, source 6 wrongUsernameErrorMessage -> expected-output (each is the expected text of a toHaveText on a validation locator). Source 9 SignInValidationMessage is unmasked UI text -> expected-output. Values stay masked

REVIEW (spec naming, not data): the JSON key names do not match where they are asserted: wrongPasswordErrorMessage is asserted on the required-USERNAME error after the empty submit, emptyUsernameBoxErrorMessage after focusing the empty username, wrongUsernameErrorMessage after a registered username with a WRONG PASSWORD. Roles are set by use, not by name

Store MaxwellsHardware: the spec runs on env.web.baseUrl (WEB_BASE_URL, webstore-z10-at), the store every migrated webstore spec runs on (same store as the approved my-account, quick-order and home-page entries)

migrate: no data value to swap; the account is declared and leased through testData.useExisting (the wrong-password attempt counts against that account, so it should be the leased account). Alternative: swap (spec unchanged), account only checked at pre-warm
Profile: every value NO_RULE or SENSITIVE (no observation FOUND); profiled false
